classification.difficultyReason: Count four square intersections and subtract their areas from the combined areas of four rectangles.

content.prompt: Four rectangles, each with length $5\text{ m}$ and width $1\text{ m}$, overlap to form the figure shown. Calculate its area.

spec.description: Two staggered vertical 5-by-1 rectangles cross two staggered horizontal 5-by-1 rectangles. The left vertical rectangle extends higher than the right, and the upper horizontal rectangle extends farther right than the lower. All four square intersections are visible through editable outlines. Uniform decorative source fill is omitted.
spec.mathematics: Four rectangles each have area 5 square metres. Each of the four separate intersections is a 1-by-1 square; no triple intersections occur.
spec.answerVisibility: The four rectangles and their intersections are supplied; no area values or solution annotations appear.

answer.short:
$16\text{ m}^2$

Subtract the four overlapping unit squares from the sum of the four rectangle areas.
answer.worked:
Each overlap is a $1\text{ m}\times1\text{ m}$ square. Subtract each of the four overlaps once so that it is not counted twice.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Total area}&=4\times(5\times1)-4\times(1\times1)\\\text{Total area}&=20-4\\\text{Total area}&=16\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$$
